not_evidence: HAND-WRITTEN. Every harvested example is a READ response and therefore carries server-set fields (owner, created_at, url, and on a task watchers/muted). This example exists because a create/update body is a DIFFERENT shape from a read: you must build it from scratch, never echo a GET back. It is not proof the platform accepts it — that is what test:e2e is for.
teaches: create_space: id must be ^\w+$ and is UPPERCASED server-side, so reference the space (and its task ids) by the uppercase form
statuses[] carry the board's presentation fields — color and complete are set on 45/45 live statuses, so omit them and the board renders a colourless column with no done state
default_status names the column new tasks land in; the status ids are what a task's `status` refers to

priorities[] need icon + icon_type + icon_color together (27/27 live priorities set all three) — priorityIconClass() reads icon_type unconditionally, so a priority without it breaks the priority dropdown
create_task: the id is SERVER-GENERATED as {SPACEID}-{n} — any id you send is ignored, and space_id must name a space that already exists
a task's status/priority must be ids from THAT space's statuses/priorities
create_comment then react_to_comment: reaction is a map { "<emoji>": true|false }, true adds and false removes
time_tracking is an estimate plus the full logs[] array — logs REPLACES rather than appends, so adding an entry is read-modify-write, and every TimeLog field (id, user, created_at) is client-supplied
a task action is a checklist item on its own subject, not a field on the task — it never appears in get_task, and today it cannot be read back at all

assignees_typo_divergence.what: Some live tasks store `asignees` (ONE s) and no `assignees` — ALEX-7 and ALEX-12 on staging do.
assignees_typo_divergence.why_it_matters: list_tasks returns the raw stored document, so the assignee shows up there; GET /workspaces/task/{id} unmarshals into the typed struct, whose tag is `assignees`, so the same task looks unassigned. The two routes disagree for the same task.
assignees_typo_divergence.the_correct_spelling: `assignees`. model/api.go Task.Assignees and UpdateTaskRequest.Assignees both use json:"assignees", so a write with the correct spelling round-trips on BOTH routes — verified live 2026-07-30 after setting the assignee on this task: get_task and list_tasks agreed, and the `asignees` key was absent.
assignees_typo_divergence.the_other_typo: hub-service/agents/agents.go:412 also declares `json:"asignees,omitempty"`, backing resolveTaskKnowledge. It only reads and re-marshals, so it is not what produced the bad records — but it does mean an agent given a `task://` knowledge URI never receives assignees for a CORRECTLY stored task.

comment.body: Broker confirmed the sum insured moves to 2.5M. Referring for underwriter sign-off.

reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.was_wrong: This example used { "eyes": true } — a shortcode NAME. That is wrong and it shipped to staging, where the comment showed a broken reaction until it was corrected.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.why: The reaction key is stored VERBATIM and rendered as-is. Nothing on the platform converts a shortcode name into a glyph.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.verified_live: 2026-07-30 on comment c_EjFPH9ZyI5. Posting { "eyes": true } returned reactions { "eyes": { count: 1, users: [...] } } — the literal string. Posting { "👀": true } returned { "👀": { count: 1, users: [...] } }. Both stored happily; only the emoji one renders.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.fix: Pass the emoji character itself. validate_payload now ERRORS on a non-emoji key.
reaction_key_must_be_a_real_emoji.also_corrected: The docs claimed a reaction needs a Bearer JWT or it is stored against an empty user id. Not so: this reaction was written with an API KEY alone and came back attributed to a real user id (the account the key resolves to).

time_tracking._user_note: user.id/user.name below are PLACEHOLDERS. The snapshot is client-supplied — the backend never fills it from the token — so a real write must carry a real uuid from list_users paired with that user's actual name, or the UI attributes the entry to nobody. tools/push-example.mjs substitutes the authenticated account's own id and name before sending. Shipping a colleague's identity inside an example file is not the way to make it render.

time_tracking_merge_semantics_verified_l.verified: 2026-07-29 against MCP_VERIFICATION_RENEWALS-1 on staging, one PATCH per case, each confirmed by re-reading the task.
time_tracking_merge_semantics_verified_l.time_tracking present without logs: existing logs PRESERVED — the nil slice marshals as "logs":null but is not destructive, which is the opposite of what the Go struct's missing omitempty suggests
time_tracking_merge_semantics_verified_l.logs: [one entry]: the array is REPLACED wholesale — the two entries that were there were gone, so this is never an append
time_tracking_merge_semantics_verified_l.consequence: adding a log is read-modify-write: get_task, take time_tracking.logs, append, send the complete array back
time_tracking_merge_semantics_verified_l.units: always seconds. The UI parses "2h 30m" using 1w=5d and 1d=8h (task-time-tracking.utils.ts) and sends only the number; totals, remaining and progress are derived client-side and must never be sent.

task_action_cannot_be_verified.symptom: PUT /workspaces/task/{task_id}/action returns 200 with the action, and GET on the same path returns 400 "description is required".
task_action_cannot_be_verified.cause: the gateway maps the GET at the WRITE resource microstrate.workspaces.put.task-action, so it invokes AddTaskActionHandler. ListTaskActionsHandler exists at workspaces-service/handler/task_actions.go:94 and is registered as get.task-actions in service/service.go, but no gateway route points at it.
task_action_cannot_be_verified.consequence: the write response is the request echoed back (response.SuccessWithBody(request, body)), not the stored aggregate — so with no read route NOTHING about a task action is verifiable, including whether a partial write merges or replaces. This is the one place in this MCP that cannot follow the read-back-after-every-write rule.
task_action_cannot_be_verified.also: no component in microstrate/src reads task actions, so an action written today is invisible in the UI as well.
task_action_cannot_be_verified.fix: repoint the GET mapping at microstrate.workspaces.get.task-actions.
task_action_cannot_be_verified.verified: 2026-07-29 on staging: PUT 200, GET 400, DELETE 200, DELETE of an unknown id 404 "resource not found", PUT against a nonexistent task 404 "task not found".
